comment: Apps the H9 Toolbox App Manager offers (dist/apps/). publish_catalog.py adds sizes, RAM, CRC and SHA-256 and copies each app to dist/apps/catalog/ as one .h9mod bundle. `name` is the main module (the menu label, 16 characters at most); `modules` lists every module the app installs, main first (default: just `name`). Names starting with '.' are hidden from the on-radio menu.

menu.name: MENU
menu.title: Module menu
menu.description: The on-radio list that opens when you hold Back. Installed automatically with the first app.
menu.summary: The on-radio list that opens when you hold Back; Back returns to the radio.
controls: Hold Back for about half a second to open it. Up/Down move, Menu runs the selection.
Back returns to the radio without a restart (needs the firmware with the return-to-radio loader); USB UPDATE starts the USB loader.
notes: Opening it also stops the SAT PASS tracker and puts your VFOs back.

apps.name: BRICK BREAKER
apps.title: Brick Breaker
apps.description: A small game that runs from the app menu. Break 30 bricks with a bouncing ball; power-cycle the radio to leave it.
apps.summary: Break 30 bricks with a bouncing ball.
controls: Menu moves the paddle left, Back moves it right.
Up restarts after GAME OVER.
notes: There is no exit key: power-cycle the radio to leave.

apps.name: MAZE CHASE
apps.title: Maze Chase
apps.summary: Eat every dot while four prowlers hunt you.
apps.description: An original maze game. Steer through a 25 by 19 maze eating every dot while four prowlers (red, pink, cyan and orange, each hunting a different way) chase you. A power pellet in each corner turns them blue for a few seconds so you can eat them for 200, 400, 800 and 1600 points. You have three lives; each level makes the prowlers faster. The tunnel in the middle row wraps from one side to the other. Sound effects play through the radio's speaker: dot munches, power pellets, eaten prowlers, a start jingle, level clear, defeat.
controls: On the title screen, 5 turns sound on or off; any other key starts.
2, 4, 6, 8 steer (up, left, right, down); Up and Down also steer up and down.
The turn you choose is taken at the next opening.
Menu pauses and resumes. Back leaves to the menu.
After GAME OVER: Menu plays again, Back leaves.
notes: Sound is experimental. It drives the speaker's DAC the way the Doom firmware does, and has not been tried inside the app loader yet. If the radio acts up, switch sound off on the title screen.
Score and best score are kept only until you leave the game.
Not tested on a radio yet.

Later in a game: lives at the top right

apps.name: APRS
apps.title: APRS
apps.description: An on-radio APRS client. The list shows the stations you hear (and starts with the stock Beacon List), each with how long ago you heard it and how far away it is. Each station has a details page, and a map draws them around your GPS position. Messages are kept (yours to you in green, and the ones you send show ACK once the other station acknowledges). SEND types and sends messages or a status packet from your callsign, and BEACON sends your position as you move (smart beaconing). The stock firmware does the transmitting.
apps.summary: APRS client: stations, map, messages, sending and smart beaconing from your GPS.
controls: The bottom line names the screens: 1 list, 2 map, 3 messages, 4 send, 5 beacon. Press the digit to jump there (holding Menu cycles list, map, messages). Back returns to the list; Back on the list leaves the app.

List: Up/Down choose a station, Menu opens its details (and from there Menu writes it a message). Rows show the call, how long ago it was heard (NOW, 5M, 2H; grey rows come from the radio's stored Beacon List) and its distance and direction from you.
Map: Up/Down zoom (1 to 500 km), Menu picks the next station. Without a GPS fix it centres on the selected station.
Messages: Up/Down choose, Menu reads. Messages sent to your callsign are green and counted as new on the list until you open Messages.
Send: type with the number keys (press a digit repeatedly to cycle its letters, 0 is space); Back deletes; Menu or Up/Down finish a field; then Menu to review and Menu again to transmit.

Beacon (screen 5, and its own entry in the radio's menu): Up/Down choose MODE, EVERY or SYMBOL and Menu changes it. MODE SMART sends as you move (about every 300 m: every 60 s at 18 km/h and faster, up to 10 min when slow; a sharp turn sends at once; one more after 30 s stopped). MODE TIMED sends every 1, 2, 5, 10, 15 or 30 minutes (EVERY). HOLD Menu for about a second to start or stop beaconing; it starts off. 5 sends one position now. Back stops and leaves. The first position goes out about 15 s after you start.
notes: Sending and beaconing are experimental. Use your own callsign (set in the radio) and keep it short. They transmit on the APRS TX channel, 2 m only; you need an amateur licence.
APRS BEACON transmits by itself while its screen is open (leaving the screen stops it), on the APRS TX channel, 2 m only. Try it with the antenna disconnected first.

With no GPS fix it beacons your last known position (this session's last fix, else the one the radio saved), marked "last known" and without course or speed. It listens to the GPS only while it runs; heard stations are not shown there.
Smart-beacon scheduling by Tomasz Kuehn (github.com/tomaszkuehn/TD-H9-aprs-smartbeacon, MIT licence).
APRS 0.7 and APRS BEACON have not been tested on a radio yet.

screenshots.caption: Station list: call, how long ago it was heard, distance and direction
Messages, with ACK on the ones you sent
Beacon: smart or timed, symbol, and start/stop

apps.name: SAT PASS
apps.title: FM Satellite Passes
apps.description: Predicts the next five passes of FM voice satellites over your GPS position, draws each pass on a sky plot, shows live Doppler-corrected frequencies, and can follow a pass by itself: it keeps VFO B on the downlink and VFO A on the uplink, sets the satellite's access tone, holds the squelch open and puts PF1 on PTT2, while the radio runs normally. Choose the satellites and refresh their orbital data in Satellite settings.
apps.summary: Next five FM satellite passes, a sky plot, and live Doppler tuning of VFO A and B.
controls: Open it from the radio's menu (hold Back). It needs GPS time and a position (or a saved fix).
LIST: Up/Down pick a pass; Menu opens the sky plot; Back exits.
PLOT: Up/Down step through the passes; Menu goes to TRACK; Back returns to the list.
TRACK: live azimuth, elevation, range and the Doppler-corrected SEND (uplink) and LISTEN (downlink) frequencies; Up/Down change pass; Back returns to the list.

TRACK, then Menu: the start screen. Up: sending on/off. Down: swap which VFO listens. 2: squelch open during the pass. 3: only this pass. 4: PF1 = PTT2. Menu: start. 1: test now (acts at once, whatever the time). Back: cancel.

After you start, the radio goes back to its normal screen and follows the pass (on older firmware it restarts first). The status bar shows AOS (time to rise) or LOS (time left). Hold Back to stop: your VFO frequencies, tones, squelch and PF1 key are put back.
notes: Times use the radio's own time zone setting.
Check amsat.org/status first: several FM satellites are intermittent or silent.
You are responsible for transmitting: low power, a suitable antenna, your licence. Try the uplink on a dummy load first.
Orbital data ages: refresh it in Satellite settings every week or two (needs a connection to CelesTrak).
If the radio loses power mid-pass, VFO A and B keep the last tracked values until you open the menu (hold Back).

screenshots.caption: Pass list: the next five passes with rise time, peak elevation, length and time to go
Sky plot of the next pass
Live track: Doppler-corrected send and listen frequencies

apps.name: GPS
apps.title: GPS Info
apps.description: Everything the radio's GPS receiver reports, on four pages: position (latitude and longitude, altitude, speed, course, satellites used, HDOP, Maidenhead grid), a sky plot of every satellite in view, signal-to-noise bars per satellite (GPS, GLONASS, Galileo, BeiDou), and time and sentence counts. Read only.
apps.summary: GPS position, sky plot, signal bars and UTC and local time.
controls: Up: previous page. Menu or Down: next page. Back: exit.
notes: The INFO page shows UTC and local time (from the radio's Time zone setting) and the last fix saved on the chip.

screenshots.caption: Sky plot of the satellites in view

apps.name: APRS MONITOR
apps.title: APRS Monitor (probe)
apps.description: First step towards an on-radio APRS client: reads packets and GPS straight from the APRS modem's serial ring and shows the last four stations heard. Receive only.
apps.summary: Receive-only probe of the APRS modem's packets and GPS.
controls: Back returns to the menu.

apps.name: VFO PROBE
apps.title: VFO Probe (research)
apps.description: A read-only research tool. Page 1 shows the radio's tuning fields, page 2 scans RAM for frequency-like values, and page 3 shows the SAT PASS tracker's status (calls, reverts, flags, squelch and PF1 bytes). It writes nothing.
apps.summary: Research: where the radio keeps its VFO frequencies, and the tracker's status.
controls: Menu: next page. On the scan page, Up/Down scroll. Back exits.
notes: Set VFO A and B to two different frequencies (for example 145.800 and 435.000) before scanning.
